messages:
maya: quick question — we've been getting a few billing tickets where customers hit huge query costs when traces get read from cold. Do we want TTLs tied to environment only (staging/prod) or to commitment level (free/paid/dedicated)?

samir: +1 to this being explicit. commitment-tier mapping lets us offer better SLAs to enterprise. staging/dev should be cheaper+shorter.

leo: curious about the fallback behavior: if hot capacity is exhausted, do we: 1) serve from cold (higher latency & cost), 2) return sampled results, or 3) enqueue rehydrate then return error?

maya: right — all 3 are in play. Current plan was (hot -> cold read) with an option to sample for low-tier orgs. But cold reads spike cost.

anya: what about a hybrid: keep a small enterprise hot buffer (based on commit level), + on-demand rehydrate with a throttled queue to limit cost. Also surface rehydrate cost per org in billing console.

samir: sounds reasonable. we need a policy schema we can attach to a customer config. something like:
```yaml
retention:
  default_env: prod
  policies:
    - selector: {env: prod, tier: enterprise}
      hot_window_days: 30
      cold_ttl_days: 365
      promote_on_query: true
      max_rehydrate_qps: 5
    - selector: {env: prod, tier: self-serve}
      hot_window_days: 7
      cold_ttl_days: 90
      promote_on_query: false
      max_rehydrate_qps: 1
```

maya: love that. two extra knobs we should consider: "cost_cap" per rehydrate job and an opt-in "aggressive_promote" for debug-mode customers.

leo: also add metric hooks: trace_query_latency_p95, cold_rehydrate_latency_p90, cold_rehydrate_cost_per_gb. We need cost telemetry to show customers the delta when they query cold traces.

devops-bot: archiver-service: started cold-compact run for bucket rds-traces-2026-03. ETA 24h.

anya: one operational gotcha: rehydrate hurts hot node memory usage (KV cache growth). maybe we should do KV warming separate from full promote. promote_on_query could be "warm_kv_only" vs "full_promote".

samir: good call. let's extend the schema with promote_mode: [none,warm_kv,full]. also implement a soft-fallback where if cold read latency > X ms we return sampled + "results_truncated" flag in API.

maya: agreed. action items: 1) samir to draft RFC with schema + prometheus metrics, 2) eng-platform to prototype warm_kv promote mode, 3) product to add rehydrate cost to billing page (anya). deadline EOW for an RFC draft?

samir: I'll put up an initial RFC tomorrow. @maya can you add a couple example org mappings so I can run sims?

maya: yup will DM examples. thanks all :thumbsup:

leo: +1, also flagging a potential console UX change: show "hot window remaining" on the trace view so PDs understand why older traces are slow.

anya: and we should include a warning in the console when a query will trigger a rehydrate with estimated cost (like a modal).

maya: perfect — will include UX mock notes in RFC.

devops-bot: deploy-bot: retention-policy-service v0.9.2 rolled out to staging.

samir: nice. I'll wire up metrics in staging and run a few synthetic cold-read tests.

maya: thanks everyone — moving this to RFC channel after I get samir's draft.
